patch_description:
The program failed validation because it broke the API contract: it returned an empty column_orderings list (no valid per-row orderings), mutated cell contents/columns (added an "original_index" column, merged/dropped columns, concatenated DataFrames with mismatched columns), relied on broken recursion (assigning rows via `result_df.loc[i]` into an empty frame, `hasattr` attribute lookups on tuples, groupby on nonexistent columns), and used a squared-length objective unrelated to the actual serial character-Trie reuse.

Fix: replace the editable algorithm with a correct, bounded implementation that (1) preserves every cell, row, and column exactly, (2) returns valid per-row column orderings consistent with the returned DataFrame, (3) constructs a few cheap candidate global column orderings (length-weighted repetition count·(count−1)·len ranking, count·(count−1) ranking, and original order), scores each with the true serial-Trie objective (sum of adjacent LCPs over sorted serialized rows, computed with C-speed slice-equality binary search), and returns the best. col_merge groups are kept contiguous in the ordering, honoring merge adjacency without altering data. NaN/mixed types are handled by normalizing only the scoring serialization string ("" for missing), never modifying stored values.
